newsitem.title: UK: LME copper flirts with $1,970 in late London.
newsitem.headline: LME copper flirts with $1,970 in late London.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three months copper flirted with strong resistance at $1,970 per tonne in late inter-office activity but by the time Comex closed at 1800 GMT a rally had not quite found the weight to breach it. It was assessed just then at $1,969. Last trade on the kerb had been at $1,958.
Copper prices had earlier pushed above $1,950 resistance with the firmer trend also assisting the aluminium market to recover from an early fresh 2-1/2 year lows.

Traders said short-term technical tightness on the LME helped copper to rally. Tightness reflects a finely balanced short-term supply/demand picture, with LME warehouse inventories expected to fall again on Friday.
Aluminium was bid at $1,336 by the hour of the Comex close after it had dropped to the new 2-1/2 year $1,305 early.
